reader.requirement: At --std 85, under DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA the comma takes the decimal-point role and the period the insertion role in every PICTURE character-string (fixed and floating insertion, check protection, CR/DB, BLANK WHEN ZERO, the decimal point counted once) and the comma is the decimal separator in every numeric literal (VALUE, MOVE, arithmetic, relation), in the program and its contained programs; a period written as a decimal point in a numeric literal is then not a numeric literal.

edition-consulted.switches: which symbols may take a repetition factor: at 85 the §1985:VI.5.9.4 GR7 list, read with the comma/period swap (under DPC the insertion period takes one and the decimal-point comma does not); 2002+ admits any symbol
the character-string length bound per edition (not DPC-specific)
lowercase folding of PICTURE letters (85 folds only the symbol letters); comma and period are not letters, so the swap is untouched
BLANK WHEN ZERO with S (2002+); not DPC-specific

reader.edition-search: grep DecimalPointIsComma/DecimalComma over src (binder, Frontend NumericLiteral and SeparatorRule, PicInfo, CobolEdit); grep DialectLevel/CobolVersion/Construct in PictureAnalyzer.cs, PictureComposition.cs, SpecialNamesBinder.cs, NumericLiteral.cs, SeparatorRule.cs: the DPC flag (SwitchBindDecimalPoint, NumericLiteral.Normalize, the edit masks) is edition-neutral; the only edition-dependent reading of the swap is RepeatableSymbol's 85 list.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: only the 85 repetition-factor list (PIC 99,(1)9 under DPC is refused at 85 with COBOL7078 and accepted at 2023); the exchange itself is the same at every edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf08_01 covers fixed insertion, the comma decimal point, numeric literals in MOVE/ADD/IF/COMPUTE; not floating insertion, check protection, CR/sign editing, BLANK WHEN ZERO, VALUE literals, de-editing, repetition of the insertion period, contained programs, or the refusals (probed here).

reader.notes: One flag (ConfigurationSlice.DecimalPointIsComma) set by SwitchBindDecimalPoint drives the literal normalizer and is captured per PICTURE clause (PicInfo.DecimalPointIsComma) for editing, de-editing and scale. DISPLAY of a numeric DISPLAY item with V prints the decimal comma, the implementor's conversion (§1985:VI.6.10.4 GR1), not this rule. Diagnostics at 85 cite §2023 clause numbers, a message-text matter.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85 under DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA. r2dpc-002 (d,f): PIC 99V.99 <- 12,34 gives [12.34] (V plus the insertion period, legal under DPC); PIC 999.99 <- 123,45 gives [001.23] (period is simple insertion, all five 9s integer); PIC ZZ9, (decimal comma last, followed by the separator period: ',.' per §1985:VI.5.9.5 GR5) <- 123,9 gives [123,]; PIC ZZ9.. (insertion period last) <- 45 gives [ 45.]; PIC ZZ.ZZZ,ZZ <- 0 gives all spaces and <- 0,05 gives [      ,05]; floating PIC $.$$$,99 <- 1,5 gives [   $1,50]; 88 VALUE 0,5 THRU 1,5 tested true for 1,25; MOVE -,5 then IF = -0,50 true; COMPUTE ROUNDED = 1,005 + +,004 gives 001,01; IF 2,7 > 2,69 true; PIC 9.999.999,99 <- 1234567,89 gives [1.234.567,89]. r2sep-002: ADD 1, 5 (comma+space is the separator) gives 006,00; ADD 1,5 2,5 gives 004,00. Refusals (b,c): r2v99V99-001 PIC 99V,99 and r2v999V9-001 PIC 9,99V9 refused COBOL1934 (V with the actual decimal point, §1985:VI.5.9.5 GR5); r2flt-001 floating literal 1,5E3 refused COBOL0900 at 85; DISPLAY 1,5 refused at 85 by §1985:VI.6.10.3 SR2 (a different rule, consistent). cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR12  (4.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR12'; 'OK  §1985:VI.5.9.5 GR5  (5.9.5 Editing Rules)  the text is in GR5' (the ',.' combination and the V/actual decimal point exclusion); 'OK  §1985:VI.5.9.4 GR8d  (5.9.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR8d' (the period/comma exchange in PICTURE).
